title: adaptive-clock-governors-kv-heatmap-playbook
summary: Experimental playbook for a short-horizon governor that adjusts GPU clocks and power caps based on a KV cache access heatmap to reduce tail latency and thermal churn across mixed-model inference pools.
scope: Redwood Dedicated and Private pools. Interaction between DVFS/clocks, platform power capping, kernel selection, and KV cache residency. Hardware: NVIDIA A100, H100, L4 and AMD MI300. Not a replacement for autoscaling or rollout policies.
motivation: Synchronized KV-miss storms and small-batch bursts cause transient SM and memory bandwidth spikes that trigger thermal/power responses and kernel fallback, producing p95/p99 latency tails and increased energy costs. Goal: smooth utilization and reduce fallback frequency while preserving throughput and tenant SLAs.
design_overview: Heatmap-driven governor: collect 1s telemetry, aggregate into a short sliding window (default 30s), compute hotness_score, burstiness_index, sustained_util, map to profile (conserve/balanced/peak/transient-boost), and actuate clocks and power caps via vendor tooling with gradual steps to avoid hysteresis.
inputs: KV cache hit/miss counters per model-version, per-node batch-size histogram, active stream counts, seq-length estimates, GPU metrics (SM util, mem bw, temps, power, clocks), kernel fallback events and kernel exec latency distributions.
heatmap_engine: Sliding-window aggregator (30s default) outputs: hotness_score (heuristic combining miss_rate, active_streams, batch_factor), burstiness_index (short-window kurtosis or percentile spread), sustained_util_percent (moving avg SM util).
policy_mapping: Policy maps (hotness_score, burstiness_index, sustained_util) -> profile. Profiles contain: clock_percent_target, power_cap_watts, kernel_preference_hint, ramp/decay params. Profiles: conserve, balanced, peak, transient-boost.
actuation: Actuate via nvidia-smi/driver APIs or rocm-smi. Apply deltas in small steps (e.g., every 5s) until profile target reached. On kernel-fallback detection, raise to peak profile immediately for a short window and then decay with hysteresis.
safety_rules: Respect per-tenant pinned minimums and model floors. Do not reduce clocks below tenant SLA floors. Auto-revert and alert on safety signals (excessive ECC errors, thermal trips, driver restarts).
per_hardware_guidance: A100: start balanced caps ~260W (80GB)/240W (40GB), balanced ~90-98% SM clock, ramp +2-4% steps. H100: start ~320W, balanced ~95% target, transient-boost on fallback, monitor HBM temps. L4: power envelopes 50-75W, balanced ~65W, favor short transient boosts and aggressive eviction/prefetch. MI300: use rocm-smi, start ~320W, adjust sclk/mclk within vendor-safe ranges, watch XGMI/HBM thermal boundaries.
scheduler_interaction: Scheduler should consult node heatmap before placing hot KV-resident segments: prefer spreading heavy segments across nodes, avoid densifying when sustained_util > 70%. Preemptively prefetch KV blocks to nodes with spare headroom when heatmap predicts rising hotness. Prefer eviction of cold segments instead of throttling when eviction reduces memory pressure.
kernel_fallback_mitigation: If fallback events exceed threshold (e.g., 5/min) for a route, escalate node to peak profile for 30s, emit alert to rollout/system. Require sustained improvement before lowering profile; use multi-step decay and require stable reduced fallback counts.
observability: Track heatmap signals (hotness_score, burstiness_index, sustained_util), actuation events (profile_change, power_cap_change_watts, clock_delta), outcomes (p50/p95/p99 latency by model-route, kernel_fallback_count, tokens/sec, energy-per-token), and safety signals (thermal_trip_events, ECC errors).
experiment_plan: 1) Canary small pool (4 GPUs) with synthetic KV-miss storms. 2) Baseline metric collection. 3) Telemetry-only validation 24-48h. 4) Stepwise policy experiments (conservative, balanced, peak) each 6-12h. 5) Stage rollout with auto-revert guardrails.
operational_checklist: Validate driver versions and manual cap application, ensure telemetry latency <2s, set per-tenant minimum clock floors, add dashboard for heatmaps and actuation timeline, configure alerts and auto-revert policies.
open_questions: Which short-window estimator is best for burstiness_index (kurtosis vs percentile spread vs EWMA variance)? Optimal decay schedule for transient-boost (exponential vs linear)? How to avoid conflicts with hardware-level automatic power management? Multi-tenant attribution and fairness?
